title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 100 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 524–529 (Night 100, continuing directly from nights-99), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 100 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. The infidels, hearing the escaped Muslims cry “God is greatest” from the mountain, fall on one another in the dark; at dawn they ride after the fugitives and surround them, and Ḍawʾ al-Makān and Sharrukān go down to fight — when the war-cry of a Muslim army answers them. It is Bahrām and Rustam with twenty thousand horse. The story turns back to tell why they came: the emir of the Turks feared for the missing king, and on the road they met the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī, disguised as an ascetic, who told them their leaders were all but lost. They rode on regardless, found the brothers alive, and all now hurry back to Constantinople while Ḍawʾ al-Makān recites a poem of thanks. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْمُوفِيَةُ لِلْمِائَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-mūfiyatu li-al-miʾati
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the completing-one for the hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the hundredth night,
sentences.n: The night is numbered “the one that completes the hundred”, the hundredth. The print spells miʾa “hundred” with an alif, مائة, the old spelling; the alif is not pronounced.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ شَرْكَانَ قَالَ أَشْتَهِي أَنْ تُوَافِقُونِي عَلَى هَذَا الرَّأْيِ وَهُوَ لَا يَكُونُ إِلَّاخَيْرًا
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna sharrukāna qāla ashtahī an tuwāfiqūnī ʿalā hādhā al-raʾyi wa-huwa lā yakūnu illā khayran
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that Sharrukān said: I desire that you agree-with-me on this counsel, and it will not be except good.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that Sharrukān said, “I would like you to go along with me in this plan; nothing but good will come of it.”
sentences.n: The print has هلى, a misprint for على, corrected here. The night opens by repeating Sharrukān’s last words from the night before. The print runs السعيد and ان together (السعيدان), and الا and خيرا (الاخيرا); the spacing is kept. wāfaqa ʿalā, “agree with (someone) on”: the verb chooses the ʿalā.

sentences.t: فَأَجَابُوهُ إِلَى ذَلِكَ وَطَلَعُوا فَوْقَ الْجَبَلِ وَصَاحُوا بِالتَّكْبِيرِ فَكَبَّرَتْ مَعَهُمُ الْجِبَالُ وَالْأَشْجَارُ وَالْأَحْجَارُ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ajābūhu ilā dhālika wa-ṭalaʿū fawqa al-jabali wa-ṣāḥū bi-al-takbīri fa-kabbarat maʿahumu al-jibālu wa-al-ashjāru wa-al-aḥjāru min khashyati allāhi
sentences.l: And they answered him to that, and climbed above the mountain and shouted with the takbīr; and with them the mountains and the trees and the stones cried “God is greatest”, from fear of God.
sentences.i: They agreed, climbed the mountain and shouted the takbīr, and the mountains, the trees and the stones cried “God is greatest” with them, in awe of God.
sentences.n: This too repeats the close of the last night. ajāba ilā, “consent to”: the verb chooses the ilā. ṣāḥa bi-, “shout (a cry)”: bi- of the words shouted. The shadda on كبّرت is the print’s.

sentences.t: فَسَمِعَهُ الْكُفَّارُ فَصَاحُوا عَلَى بَعْضِهِمْ وَلَبِسُوا السِّلَاحَ وَقَالُوا قَدْ هَجَمَتْ عَلَيْنَا الْأَعْدَاءُ وَحَقِّ الْمَسِيحِ
sentences.tr: fa-samiʿahu al-kuffāru fa-ṣāḥū ʿalā baʿḍihim wa-labisū al-silāḥa wa-qālū qad hajamat ʿalaynā al-aʿdāʾu wa-ḥaqqi al-masīḥi
sentences.l: And the infidels heard it, and they shouted to one-another, and put-on the weapons, and said: The enemies have rushed upon us, by the truth of the Messiah!
sentences.i: The infidels heard it and called out to one another and took up their arms, saying, “By the Messiah, the enemy is upon us!”
sentences.n: -hu, “it”, is the takbīr. ṣāḥa ʿalā, “call out to”: the verb chooses the ʿalā. labisa al-silāḥa, “put on the weapons”, is to arm oneself. hajama ʿalā, “rush upon”; hajamat is feminine with al-aʿdāʾ, a broken plural. wa-ḥaqqi al-masīḥi, “by the truth of the Messiah”: the wa- of oaths, which takes the genitive.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَتَلُوا مِنْ بَعْضِهِمْ مَا لَا يَعْلَمُ عَدَدَهُ إِلَّااللَّهُ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: thumma qatalū min baʿḍihim mā lā yaʿlamu ʿadadahu illā allāhu taʿālā
sentences.l: Then they killed of one-another what none knows its number except God, exalted-is-He.
sentences.i: Then they killed so many of one another that none but God Most High knows the number.
sentences.n: The print runs الا and الله together (الاالله); the spacing is kept. In the dark and the drink they fell on each other, as Sharrukān had foreseen. mā … ʿadadahu, “what … its number”: the -hu picks up the mā.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ الصَّبَاحُ فَتَّشُوا عَلَى الْأَسَارَى فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا لَهُمْ أَثَرًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna al-ṣabāḥu fattashū ʿalā al-asārā fa-lam yajidū lahum atharan
sentences.l: And when it was the morning, they searched for the captives, and did not find of them a trace.
sentences.i: When morning came they searched for the prisoners, but found no trace of them.
sentences.n: fattasha ʿalā, “search for”, is the text’s usage, where Classical says fattasha ʿan; the shadda is the print’s. lahum, “of them”: li- of whom the trace belongs to.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ رُؤَسَاؤُهُمْ إِنَّ الَّذِي فَعَلَ بِكُمْ هَذِهِ الْفِعْلَ هُمُ الْأَسَارَى الَّذِينَ كَانُوا عِنْدَنَا بِدُونَكُمْ وَالسَّعْيَ خَلْفَكُمْ حَتَّى تَلْحَقُوهُمْ فَتَسْقُوهُمْ كَأْسَ الْوَبَالِ وَلَا يَحْصُلُ لَكُمْ خَوْفٌ وَلَا انْذِهَالٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ruʾasāʾuhum inna alladhī faʿala bikum hādhihi al-fiʿla humu al-asārā alladhīna kānū ʿindanā bi-dūnakum wa-al-saʿya khalfakum ḥattā talḥaqūhum fa-tasqūhum kaʾsa al-wabāli wa-lā yaḥṣulu lakum khawfun wa-lā indhihālun
sentences.l: And their chiefs said: The-one-who did to you this deed, they are the captives who were with us. At-it-you! — and the running behind-you, until you overtake them and give-them-to-drink the cup of the ruin; and there will not come-about to you fear nor bewilderment.
sentences.i: Their chiefs said, “The ones who did this to you are the prisoners we were holding. After them! Run them down until you catch them and make them drink the cup of ruin, and have neither fear nor dismay.”
sentences.n: The print has هذة, a misprint for هذه, corrected here. hādhihi is feminine with the masculine al-fiʿl, “the deed”: the text’s own agreement. بدونكم is doubtful. The letters could be read bi-dūnikum, “without you”, which makes no sense here; they are read here as dūnakum, “to it, at them!”, the word that urges men on and takes its object in the accusative (al-saʿya, “the running”), with a bi- in front of it. خلفكم, “behind you”, is also as printed, where the sense wants خلفهم, “behind them”. faʿala bi-, “do to”: the verb chooses the bi-. kaʾs al-wabāl, “the cup of ruin”, is death. Sajʿ: al-wabāli/indhihālun.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ رَكِبُوا خُيُولَهُمْ وَسَعَوْا خَلْفَهُمْ فَمَا كَانَ إِلَّا لَحْظَةٌ حَتَّى لَحِقُوهُمْ وَأَحَاطُوا بِهِمْ
sentences.tr: thumma innahum rakibū khuyūlahum wa-saʿaw khalfahum fa-mā kāna illā laḥẓatun ḥattā laḥiqūhum wa-aḥāṭū bihim
sentences.l: Then they mounted their horses and ran behind them, and there was not but a glance until they overtook them and surrounded them.
sentences.i: Then they mounted their horses and went after them, and it was only a moment before they had caught them up and surrounded them.
sentences.n: laḥẓa is a glance, the blink of an eye. aḥāṭa bi-, “surround”: the verb chooses the bi-.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَى ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ ذَلِكَ ازْدَادَ بِهِ الْفَزَعُ وَقَالَ لِأَخِيهِ إِنَّ الَّذِي خِفْتُ مِنْ حُصُولِهِ قَدْ حَصَلَ وَمَا بَقِيَ لَنَا حَيَاةٌ إِلَّا الْجِهَادُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā ḍawʾu al-makāni dhālika izdāda bihi al-fazaʿu wa-qāla li-akhīhi inna alladhī khiftu min ḥuṣūlihi qad ḥaṣala wa-mā baqiya lanā ḥayātun illā al-jihādu
sentences.l: And when Ḍawʾ al-Makān saw that, the terror increased in him, and he said to his brother: That which I feared of its coming-about has come-about, and there remains not to us a life except the holy-war.
sentences.i: When Ḍawʾ al-Makān saw this his dread grew, and he said to his brother, “What I feared would happen has happened; nothing is left for us now but to fight for the faith.”
sentences.n: The print has خنت, a misprint for خفت, “I feared”, corrected here. izdāda bihi, “grew in him”: bi- of the one it seizes. ḥayātun, “life”, is as printed, but the sense would sooner have ḥīlatun (حيلة), “resource, way out”: “no way out is left us but the jihād”. baqiya is masculine before the feminine ḥayāt, as often when the verb comes first. jihād is war for the faith.

sentences.t: فَلَزِمَ شَرْكَانُ السُّكُوتَ عَنِ الْمَقَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-lazima sharrukānu al-sukūta ʿani al-maqāli
sentences.l: And Sharrukān kept the silence from the speech.
sentences.i: Sharrukān held his peace and said nothing.
sentences.n: lazima, “cleave to, keep to”; ʿan, “from”: he kept back from speaking.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ انْحَدَرَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ مِنْ أَعْلَا الْجَبَلِ وَكَبَّرَ وَكَبَّرَتْ مَعَهُ الرِّجَالُ وَعَوَّلُوا عَلَى الْجِهَادِ وَبَاعُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ فِي طَاعَةِ رَبِّ الْعِبَادِ
sentences.tr: thumma inḥadara ḍawʾu al-makāni min aʿlā al-jabali wa-kabbara wa-kabbarat maʿahu al-rijālu wa-ʿawwalū ʿalā al-jihādi wa-bāʿū anfusahum fī ṭāʿati rabbi al-ʿibādi
sentences.l: Then Ḍawʾ al-Makān descended from the top of the mountain and cried “God is greatest”, and the men cried it with him, and they resolved upon the holy-war and sold themselves in the obedience of the Lord of the servants.
sentences.i: Then Ḍawʾ al-Makān came down from the mountain top crying “God is greatest”, and the men cried it with him; they set their minds on holy war and sold their lives in obedience to the Lord of all who serve Him.
sentences.n: The print spells aʿlā with a final alif, اعلا; the spelling is kept. ʿawwala ʿalā, “resolve on”: the verb chooses the ʿalā. Selling one’s self to God is Qurʾānic (Q 9:111). The shaddas are the print’s. Sajʿ: al-jihādi/al-ʿibādi.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَاهُمْ كَذَلِكَ وَإِذَا بِأَصْوَاتٍ يَصِيحُونَ بِالتَّهْلِيلِ وَالتَّكْبِيرِ وَالصَّلٰوةِ وَالسَّلَامِ عَلَى الْبَشِيرِ النَّذِيرِ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamāhum ka-dhālika wa-idhā bi-aṣwātin yaṣīḥūna bi-al-tahlīli wa-al-takbīri wa-al-ṣalāti wa-al-salāmi ʿalā al-bashīri al-nadhīri
sentences.l: And while-they were thus, and behold, voices crying with the tahlīl and the takbīr and the blessing and the peace upon the bringer-of-good-news, the warner.
sentences.i: While they were so, all at once there were voices crying “There is no god but God” and “God is greatest”, calling blessing and peace upon the Bearer of good tidings, the Warner.
sentences.n: The print has النذيز, a misprint for النذير, corrected here. The print runs بينما and هم together (فبينماهم); the spacing is kept. wa-idhā bi-: after idhā of surprise the bi- only marks what appears. yaṣīḥūna, masculine plural, goes with the men behind the voices; ṣāḥa bi-, “cry (words)”: bi- of what is cried. tahlīl is saying lā ilāha illā allāh. ṣalāt is printed صلٰوة, with the dagger alif. al-bashīr al-nadhīr, “the bringer of good news, the warner”, is the Prophet, in Qurʾānic words (Q 2:119). Sajʿ: al-takbīri/al-nadhīri.

sentences.t: فَالْتَفَتُوا إِلَى جِهَةِ الصَّوْتِ فَرَأَوْا جُيُوشَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَعَسَاكِرَ الْمُوَحِّدِينَ مُقْبِلِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-iltafatū ilā jihati al-ṣawti fa-raʾaw juyūsha al-muslimīna wa-ʿasākira al-muwaḥḥidīna muqbilīna
sentences.l: And they turned to the direction of the sound, and saw the armies of the Muslims and the troops of the declarers-of-the-One coming-on.
sentences.i: They turned toward the sound and saw the armies of the Muslims, the hosts of those who proclaim God’s oneness, advancing.
sentences.n: muwaḥḥidūn, “those who declare God one”, is a name for the Muslims; the shadda is the print’s. Sajʿ: al-muslimīna/al-muwaḥḥidīna/muqbilīna.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُمْ قَوِيَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَحَمَلَ شَرْكَانُ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ وَهَلَّلَ وَكَبَّرَ هُوَ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ مِنَ الْمُوَحِّدِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾawhum qawiyat qulūbuhum wa-ḥamala sharrukānu ʿalā al-kāfirīna wa-hallala wa-kabbara huwa wa-man maʿahu mina al-muwaḥḥidīna
sentences.l: And when they saw them, their hearts grew-strong, and Sharrukān charged upon the unbelievers, and cried “No god but God” and “God is greatest”, he and who was with him of the declarers-of-the-One.
sentences.i: At the sight their hearts grew strong. Sharrukān charged the unbelievers, he and the believers with him crying “There is no god but God” and “God is greatest”.
sentences.n: ḥamala ʿalā, “charge (at)”: the verb chooses the ʿalā. hallala is to say lā ilāha illā allāh, as kabbara is to say allāhu akbar. Sajʿ: al-kāfirīna/al-muwaḥḥidīna.

sentences.t: فَارْتَجَّتِ الْأَرْضُ كَالزَّلَازِلِ وَتَفَرَّقَتْ عَسَاكِرُ الْكُفَّارِ فِي عَرْضِ الْجِبَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-irtajjati al-arḍu ka-al-zalāzili wa-tafarraqat ʿasākiru al-kuffāri fī ʿarḍi al-jibāli
sentences.l: And the earth shook like the earthquakes, and the troops of the infidels scattered in the breadth of the mountains.
sentences.i: The earth quaked as in an earthquake, and the infidel troops scattered across the mountains.
sentences.n: ka-, “like”. fī ʿarḍi, “in the breadth of”, is “all across”.

sentences.t: فَتَبِعَتْهُمُ الْمُسْلِمُونَ بِالضَّرْبِ وَالطِّعَانِ وَأَزَاحُوا مِنْهُمُ الرُّؤُسَ عَنِ الْأَبْدَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-tabiʿathumu al-muslimūna bi-al-ḍarbi wa-al-ṭiʿāni wa-azāḥū minhumu al-ruʾūsa ʿani al-abdāni
sentences.l: And the Muslims followed them with the striking and the thrusting, and removed of them the heads from the bodies.
sentences.i: The Muslims pursued them, cutting and thrusting, and parted their heads from their bodies.
sentences.n: tabiʿat is feminine with al-muslimūn, as if “the host of the Muslims”: the text’s own agreement. bi-al-ḍarbi, “with the striking”: bi- of the manner. The print spells ruʾūs “heads” with a single wāw, الرؤس. Sajʿ: al-ṭiʿāni/al-abdāni.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلْ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ هُوَ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ يَضْرِبُونَ فِي أَعْنَاقِ الْكَافِرِينَ إِلَى أَنْ وَلَّى النَّهَارُ وَأَقْبَلَ اللَّيْلُ بِالِاعْتِكَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazal ḍawʾu al-makāni huwa wa-man maʿahu mina al-muslimīna yaḍribūna fī aʿnāqi al-kāfirīna ilā an wallā al-nahāru wa-aqbala al-laylu bi-al-iʿtikāri
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān, he and who was with him of the Muslims, did not cease striking in the necks of the unbelievers until the day turned-away and the night came-on with the darkening.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān and the Muslims with him went on smiting the necks of the unbelievers until the day turned away and night came on in its darkness.
sentences.n: lam yazal with an imperfect, “did not cease doing”; yaḍribūna is plural, for the whole company. ḍaraba fī, “strike into”. aqbala bi-, “come on with”: bi- of what it brings. The same rhyming close as the night before: al-nahāru/al-iʿtikāri.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ انْحَازَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ إِلَى بَعْضِهِمْ وَبَاتُوا مُسْتَبْشِرِينَ طُولَ لَيْلِهِمْ
sentences.tr: thumma inḥāza al-muslimūna ilā baʿḍihim wa-bātū mustabshirīna ṭūla laylihim
sentences.l: Then the Muslims drew-aside to some-of-them, and they passed-the-night rejoicing the length of their night.
sentences.i: Then the Muslims drew together, and spent the whole night in gladness.
sentences.n: The print has اى, a misprint for الى, corrected here. inḥāza ilā, “withdraw to, rally to”: those who had been scattered gathered to the rest. bāta, “spend the night (doing)”, takes the participle mustabshirīna, “rejoicing at good tidings”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ وَأَشْرَقَ بِنُورِهِ وَلَاحَ رأَوْا بَهْرَامَ مُقَدَّمَ الدَّيْلَمِ وَرُسْتُمَ مُقَدَّمَ الْأَتْرَاكِ وَمَعَهُمَا عِشْرُونَ أَلْفَ فَارِسٍ مُقْبِلِينَ عَلَيْهِمْ كَاللُّيُوثِ الْعَوَابِسِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu wa-ashraqa bi-nūrihi wa-lāḥa raʾaw bahrāma muqaddama al-daylami wa-rustuma muqaddama al-atrāki wa-maʿahumā ʿishrūna alfa fārisin muqbilīna ʿalayhim ka-al-luyūthi al-ʿawābisi
sentences.l: And when the morning became-morning and shone with its light and gleamed, they saw Bahrām, the commander of the Daylam, and Rustam, the commander of the Turks, and with the two of them twenty thousand horsemen, coming-on toward them like the lions, the scowling-ones.
sentences.i: And when morning came, and shone out with its light and gleamed, they saw Bahrām, commander of the Daylam, and Rustam, commander of the Turks, bearing down on them with twenty thousand horsemen like scowling lions.
sentences.n: The print has بنورة, a misprint for بنوره, “with its light”, corrected here. aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu … wa-lāḥa is the stock daybreak formula; the rhyme falls on ṣabāḥu/lāḥa. ashraqa bi-, “shine with”: bi- of what it gives out. muqaddam, “one put in front”, is a commander. The Daylam are the people of the mountains south of the Caspian. ka-, “like”; luyūth (sing. layth) and ʿawābis (sing. ʿābis, “frowning”) are both broken plurals.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رأَوْا ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ تَرَجَّلَ الْفُرْسَانُ وَسَلَّمُوا عَلَيْهِ وَقَبَّلُوا الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾaw ḍawʾa al-makāni tarajjala al-fursānu wa-sallamū ʿalayhi wa-qabbalū al-arḍa bayna yadayhi
sentences.l: And when they saw Ḍawʾ al-Makān, the horsemen dismounted and greeted him and kissed the ground between his two hands.
sentences.i: When they saw Ḍawʾ al-Makān, the horsemen dismounted, greeted him, and kissed the ground before him.
sentences.n: tarajjala, “go on foot, dismount”, is singular before its plural subject, as usual when the verb comes first; the shadda is the print’s. sallama ʿalā, “greet”: the verb chooses the ʿalā. bayna yadayhi, “between his hands”, is “before him, in his presence”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمْ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ أَبْشِرُوا بِنَصْرِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَهَلَاكِ قَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahum ḍawʾu al-makāni abshirū bi-naṣri al-muslimīna wa-halāki qawmi al-kāfirīna
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to them: Rejoice-at-the-tidings of the victory of the Muslims and the perishing of the people of the unbelievers!
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to them, “Rejoice in the news: the Muslims are victorious and the infidel host is destroyed!”
sentences.n: abshara bi-, “receive good news of, rejoice at”: the verb chooses the bi-. Sajʿ: al-muslimīna/al-kāfirīna.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ هَنَّوْا بَعْضَهُمْ بِالسَّلَامَةِ وَعَظِيمِ الْأَجْرِ فِى الْقِيَامَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma hannaw baʿḍahum bi-al-salāmati wa-ʿaẓīmi al-ajri fī al-qiyāmati
sentences.l: Then they congratulated some-of-them on the safety and the greatness of the reward in the Resurrection.
sentences.i: Then they wished one another joy of their safe deliverance, and of the great reward awaiting them on the Day of Resurrection.
sentences.n: hannaw is hannaʾa, “congratulate”, with its hamza dropped and conjugated like a weak verb, a Middle Arabic habit; the shadda is the print’s. baʿḍahum alone stands for “one another”, where Classical would say baʿḍuhum baʿḍan. hannaʾa bi-, “congratulate on”: the verb chooses the bi-. ʿaẓīmi al-ajri, “the great of the reward”, puts the adjective first in construct. Sajʿ: al-salāmati/al-qiyāmati.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ السَّبَبُ فِي مَجِيئِهِمْ إِلَى هَذَا الْمَكَانِ أَنَّ الْأَمِيرَ بَهْرَامَ وَالْأَمِيرَ رُسْتُمَ وَالْحَاجِبَ الْكَبِيرَ لَمَّا سَارُوا بِجُيُوشِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَالرَّايَاتُ عَلَى رُؤُسِهِمْ مَنْشُورَةٌ حَتَّى وَصَلُوا إِلَى الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ رأَوُا الْكُفَّارَ قَدْ طَلَعُوا عَلَى الْأَسْوَارِ وَمَلَكُوا الْأَبْرَاجَ وَالْقِلَاعَ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-sababu fī majīʾihim ilā hādhā al-makāni anna al-amīra bahrāma wa-al-amīra rustuma wa-al-ḥājiba al-kabīra lammā sārū bi-juyūshi al-muslimīna wa-al-rāyātu ʿalā ruʾūsihim manshūratun ḥattā waṣalū ilā al-qusṭanṭīniyyati raʾawu al-kuffāra qad ṭalaʿū ʿalā al-aswāri wa-malakū al-abrāja wa-al-qilāʿa
sentences.l: And the cause of their coming to this place was that the emir Bahrām and the emir Rustam and the Chamberlain, the great-one, when they went with the armies of the Muslims, and the banners over their heads spread-out, until they reached Constantinople, they saw the infidels had climbed onto the walls and held the towers and the strongholds,
sentences.i: Now this is why they had come to that place. When the emir Bahrām, the emir Rustam and the Grand Chamberlain marched with the Muslim armies, banners unfurled above their heads, and came to Constantinople, they saw that the infidels had manned the walls and taken the towers and the citadels,
sentences.n: lammā … raʾawu: the “when” clause runs on through ḥattā waṣalū, “until they reached”, before its answer raʾawu, “they saw”, arrives. sāra bi-, “march with, lead”: bi- of what goes with them. wa-al-rāyātu … manshūratun is a circumstantial clause, “the banners being spread”. رؤسهم is the edition’s spelling of ruʾūsihim with one wāw.

sentences.t: وَاسْتَعَدُّوا فِي كُلِّ حِصْنٍ مَنَّاعٍ حِينَ عَلِمُوا بِقُدُومِ الْعَسَاكِرِ الْإِسْلَامِيَّةِ وَالْأَعْلَامِ الْمُحَمَّدِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: wa-istaʿaddū fī kulli ḥiṣnin mannāʿin ḥīna ʿalimū bi-qudūmi al-ʿasākiri al-islāmiyyati wa-al-aʿlāmi al-muḥammadiyyati
sentences.l: and made-ready in every fortress, a strong-barring-one, when they knew of the coming of the troops, the Islamic-ones, and the standards, the Muḥammadan-ones.
sentences.i: and stood ready in every impregnable fort, as soon as they learned that the troops of Islam and the standards of Muḥammad were approaching.
sentences.n: mannāʿ, “much-withholding”, is a fort that keeps out all comers; the shadda is the print’s, as on al-muḥammadiyyati. ʿalima bi-, “learn of”: the verb chooses the bi-. Sajʿ: al-qilāʿa/mannāʿin, then al-islāmiyyati/al-muḥammadiyyati.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ سَمِعُوا قَعْقَعَةَ السِّلَاحِ وَضَجَّةَ الصِّيَاحِ وَنَظَرُوا فَرأَوُا الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَسَمِعُوا حَوَافِرَ خُيُولِهِمْ مِنْ تَحْتِ الْغُبَارِ فَإِذَاهُمْ كَالْجَرَادِ الْمُنْتَشِرِ وَالسَّحَابِ الْمُنْهَمِرِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad samiʿū qaʿqaʿata al-silāḥi wa-ḍajjata al-ṣiyāḥi wa-naẓarū fa-raʾawu al-muslimīna wa-samiʿū ḥawāfira khuyūlihim min taḥti al-ghubāri fa-idhā hum ka-al-jarādi al-muntashiri wa-al-saḥābi al-munhamiri
sentences.l: And they had heard the clatter of the weapons and the clamour of the shouting, and they looked and saw the Muslims, and heard the hooves of their horses from beneath the dust, and behold, they were like the locusts, the spreading-ones, and the clouds, the pouring-ones.
sentences.i: They had heard the clash of arms and the din of battle-cries; they looked out and saw the Muslims, and heard their horses’ hooves beneath the dust, and there they were, like swarming locusts, like clouds pouring down rain.
sentences.n: The print runs فاذا and هم together (فاذاهم); the spacing is kept. fa-idhā hum, “and behold, they …”: idhā of surprise. ka-, “like”. al-jarād al-muntashir echoes Q 54:7, ka-annahum jarādun muntashirun, “as though they were scattered locusts”, and munhamir Q 54:11, “water pouring down”. Sajʿ: al-silāḥi/al-ṣiyāḥi, then al-muntashiri/al-munhamiri.

sentences.t: وَسَمِعُوا أَصْوَاتَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ بِتِلَاوَةِ الْقُرْآنِ وَتَسْبِيحِ الرَّحْمَنِ
sentences.tr: wa-samiʿū aṣwāta al-muslimīna bi-tilāwati al-qurʾāni wa-tasbīḥi al-raḥmāni
sentences.l: And they heard the voices of the Muslims with the reciting of the Qurʾān and the glorifying of the Merciful.
sentences.i: And they heard the voices of the Muslims reciting the Qurʾān and giving glory to the Merciful.
sentences.n: bi-tilāwati, “with the reciting”: bi- of what the voices were busy with. Sajʿ: al-qurʾāni/al-raḥmāni.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ السَّبَبُ فِي إِعْلَامِ الْكُفَّارِ بِذَلِكَ مَا دَبَّرَتْهُ الْعَجُوزُ ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي مِنْ زُورِهَا وَعُهْرِهَا وَبُهْتَانِهَا وَمَكْرِهَا حَتَّى قَرُبَتِ الْعَسَاكِرُ كَالْبَحْرِ الزَّاخِرِ مِنْ كَثْرَةِ الرِّجَالِ وَالْفُرْسَانِ وَالنِّسَاءِ وَالصِّبْيَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-sababu fī iʿlāmi al-kuffāri bi-dhālika mā dabbarathu al-ʿajūzu dhātu al-dawāhī min zūrihā wa-ʿuhrihā wa-buhtānihā wa-makrihā ḥattā qarubati al-ʿasākiru ka-al-baḥri al-zākhiri min kathrati al-rijāli wa-al-fursāni wa-al-nisāʾi wa-al-ṣibyāni
sentences.l: And the cause in the informing of the infidels of that was what the old-woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī had contrived, of her falsehood and her whoring and her slander and her guile, until the armies drew-near like the swelling sea, from the multitude of the men and the horsemen and the women and the boys.
sentences.i: The infidels had come to know of all this through the schemes of the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī, her lies, her harlotry, her slander and her cunning; and so their hosts had drawn near like the swelling sea, so many were the men and horsemen, the women and children.
sentences.n: iʿlām al-kuffāri bi-dhālika, “the informing of the infidels of that”: aʿlama bi-, “inform of”, the verb chooses the bi-. The sentence is loosely built and does not say exactly what “that” was; the hosts that draw near, with their women and children, are the people of Constantinople, as the emir’s words below show. Dhāt al-Dawāhī means “she of the calamities”. ka-, “like”. Sajʿ: al-zākhiri, then al-ṣibyāni rhyming back on al-qurʾāni/al-raḥmāni above.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَمِيرُ التُّرْكِ لِأَمِيرِ الدَّيْلَمِ يَا أَمِيرُ إِنَّنَا بَقِينَا عَلَى خَطَرٍ مِنَ الْأَعْدَاءِ الَّذِينَ فَوْقَ الْأَسْوَارِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla amīru al-turki li-amīri al-daylami yā amīru innanā baqīnā ʿalā khaṭarin mina al-aʿdāʾi alladhīna fawqa al-aswāri
sentences.l: And the emir of the Turks said to the emir of the Daylam: O emir, we have remained in danger from the enemies who are above the walls.
sentences.i: Then the emir of the Turks said to the emir of the Daylam, “O emir, we are left in danger from the enemy up on the walls.
sentences.n: The emir of the Turks is Rustam, the emir of the Daylam Bahrām; both are named a little further on. li-amīri, “to the emir”: li- marks whom he speaks to.

sentences.t: فَانْظُرْ إِلَى تِلْكَ الْأَبْرَاجِ وَإِلَى هَذَا الْعَالَمِ الَّذِي كَالْبَحْرِ الْعَجَّاجِ الْمُتَلَاطِمِ بِالْأَمْوَاجِ
sentences.tr: fa-unẓur ilā tilka al-abrāji wa-ilā hādhā al-ʿālami alladhī ka-al-baḥri al-ʿajjāji al-mutalāṭimi bi-al-amwāji
sentences.l: So look at those towers, and at this world which is like the roaring sea, the clashing with the waves.
sentences.i: Look at those towers, and at this multitude, like a roaring sea dashing its waves together.
sentences.n: al-ʿālam, “the world”, is used for a great crowd of people. al-mutalāṭimi bi-al-amwāji, “clashing with the waves”: bi- of the waves that clash. Sajʿ: al-abrāji/al-ʿajjāji/al-amwāji.

sentences.t: إِنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ الْكُفَّارَ قَدْرُنَا مِائَةَ مَرَّةٍ وَلَانَأْمَنُ مِنْ جَاسُوسٍ يُخْبِرُهُمْ أَنْ مَاعِنْدَنَا مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ
sentences.tr: inna hāʾulāʾi al-kuffāra qadrunā miʾata marratin wa-lā naʾmanu min jāsūsin yukhbiruhum an mā ʿindanā min sulṭānin
sentences.l: These infidels are our measure a hundred times; and we are not safe from a spy telling them that there is not with us any sultan,
sentences.i: These infidels are a hundred times our number, and we cannot be sure that some spy will not tell them that we have no sultan with us,
sentences.n: The print sets ولا and نأمن as one word (ولانأمن), and ما and عندنا as one (ماعندنا); the spacing is kept. qadrunā miʾata marratin, “our measure a hundred times”: a hundred times as many as we are. amina min, “feel safe from”. an here is anna lightened, before a clause negated with mā; min sulṭānin, “any sultan”, the min after a negative meaning “any at all”.

sentences.t: وَأَنَّنَا عَلَى خَطَرٍ مِنَ الْأَعْدَاءِ الَّذِينَ لَا يُحْصَى عَدَدُهُمْ وَلَا يَنْقَطِعُ مَدَدُهُمْ خُصُوصًا مَعَ غَيْبَةِ الْمَلِكِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَأَخِيهِ وَالْوَزِيرِ الْأَجَلِّ دَنْدَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-annanā ʿalā khaṭarin mina al-aʿdāʾi alladhīna lā yuḥṣā ʿadaduhum wa-lā yanqaṭiʿu madaduhum khuṣūṣan maʿa ghaybati al-maliki ḍawʾi al-makāni wa-akhīhi wa-al-wazīri al-ajalli dandāna
sentences.l: and that we are in danger from the enemies whose number is not counted and whose reinforcement is not cut off, especially with the absence of King Ḍawʾ al-Makān and his brother and the most-illustrious vizier Dandān.
sentences.i: and that we stand in danger from an enemy beyond counting, whose reinforcements never cease — above all with King Ḍawʾ al-Makān, his brother and the illustrious vizier Dandān away from us.
sentences.n: Sajʿ: ʿadaduhum/madaduhum. wa-annanā still hangs on what the spy would tell them.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ يَطْمَعُونَ فِينَا لِغَيْبَتِهِمْ عَنَّا فَيَمْحَقُونَنَا بِالسَّيْفِ عَنْ آخِرِنَا وَلَا يَنْجُو مِنَّا نَاجٍ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika yaṭmaʿūna fīnā li-ghaybatihim ʿannā fa-yamḥaqūnanā bi-al-sayfi ʿan ākhirinā wa-lā yanjū minnā nājin
sentences.l: And at that they will covet in us, for their absence from us, and they will annihilate us with the sword to our last, and there will not escape from us an escaper.
sentences.i: Then they will set their hopes on us, since those three are gone from us, and put us all to the sword to the last man, and not one of us will escape.
sentences.n: ṭamiʿa fī, “covet, have designs on”: the verb chooses the fī. li-ghaybatihim, “because of their absence”: li- of the cause. bi-al-sayfi, “with the sword”: bi- of the instrument. ʿan ākhirinā, “to the last of us”, is a fixed phrase. lā yanjū minnā nājin, “no escaper of us shall escape”, repeats the root for emphasis.

sentences.t: وَمِنَ الرَّأْىِ أَنْ تَأْخُذَ أَنْتَ عَشَرَةَ آلَافِ فَارِسٍ مِنَ الْمَوَاصِلَةِ وَالْأَتْرَاكِ وَتَذْهَبَ بِهِمْ إِلَى دَيْرِ مَطْرُوحَنَى وَمَرْجِ مَاوَخْنَا فِي طَلَبِ إِخْوَانِنَا وَأَصْحَابِنَا
sentences.tr: wa-mina al-raʾyi an taʾkhudha anta ʿasharata ālāfi fārisin mina al-mawāṣilati wa-al-atrāki wa-tadhhaba bihim ilā dayri maṭrūḥanā wa-marji māwakhnā fī ṭalabi ikhwāninā wa-aṣḥābinā
sentences.l: And of the counsel is that you take, you, ten thousands of horseman from the Mosul-men and the Turks, and go with them to the monastery of Maṭrūḥanā and the meadow of Māwakhnā in search of our brothers and our companions.
sentences.i: The wise course is for you to take ten thousand horsemen of the men of Mosul and the Turks, and ride with them to the monastery of Maṭrūḥanā and the meadow of Māwakhnā in search of our brothers and comrades.
sentences.n: al-mawāṣila are the men of Mosul (al-Mawṣil). dhahaba bi-, “go with, take along”: bi- of company. Dayr Maṭrūḥanā is the monastery of the monk Maṭrūḥanā met earlier. The meadow’s name is given as printed; its pointing is not certain.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ أَطَعْتُمُونِي كُنْتُمْ سَبَبًا فِى الْفَرَجِ عَنْهُمْ إِنْ كَانَ الْكُفَّارُ قَدْ ضَيَّقُوا عَلَيْهِمْ وَإِنْ لَمْ تُطِيعُونِي فَلَا لَوْمَ عَلَيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-in aṭaʿtumūnī kuntum sababan fī al-faraji ʿanhum in kāna al-kuffāru qad ḍayyaqū ʿalayhim wa-in lam tuṭīʿūnī fa-lā lawma ʿalayya
sentences.l: And if you obey me, you will be a cause in the relief from them, if the infidels have pressed upon them; and if you do not obey me, then no blame upon me.
sentences.i: If you heed me, you will be the means of their relief, should the infidels have them hard pressed; and if you do not, the blame is not mine.
sentences.n: The speech moves from “you” singular to “you” plural, taking in Bahrām’s men. al-faraj ʿanhum, “the relief from (their trouble)”. ḍayyaqa ʿalā, “press hard, hem in”: the verb chooses the ʿalā.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا تَوَجَّهْتُمْ يَنْبَغِي أَنْ تَرْجِعُوا إِلَيْنَا مُسْرِعِينَ فَإِنَّ مِنَ الْحَزْمِ سُوءَ الظَّنِّ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā tawajjahtum yanbaghī an tarjiʿū ilaynā musriʿīna fa-inna mina al-ḥazmi sūʾa al-ẓanni
sentences.l: And when you have set-out, it is fitting that you return to us hastening; for of the prudence is the ill thinking.
sentences.i: And once you have set out, you must come back to us with all speed; for suspicion is part of prudence.”
sentences.n: inna mina al-ḥazmi sūʾa al-ẓanni, “part of prudence is to think ill (of things)”, is a proverb.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَهَا قَبِلَ الْأَمِيرُ الْمَذْكُورُ كَلَامَهُ وَانْتَخَبَا عِشْرِينَ أَلْفَ فَارِسٍ وَسَارُوا يَقْطَعُونَ الطُّرُقَاتِ طَالِبِينَ الْمَرْجَ الْمَذْكُورَ وَالدَّيْرَ الْمَشْهُورَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿindahā qabila al-amīru al-madhkūru kalāmahu wa-intakhabā ʿishrīna alfa fārisin wa-sārū yaqṭaʿūna al-ṭuruqāti ṭālibīna al-marja al-madhkūra wa-al-dayra al-mashhūra
sentences.l: And thereupon the emir aforesaid accepted his speech, and the two chose twenty thousand horseman, and they went cutting the roads, seeking the meadow aforesaid and the monastery, the famous-one.
sentences.i: So the emir accepted his advice. The two of them picked out twenty thousand horsemen, who set off along the roads, making for the meadow and the famous monastery.
sentences.n: Rustam proposed ten thousand; the force chosen is twenty thousand, as printed. intakhabā is dual, the two emirs; sārū is plural, the horsemen. qaṭaʿa al-ṭuruqāt, “cut the roads”, is to travel them. Sajʿ: al-madhkūra/al-mashhūra.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ سَبَبِ مَجِيئِهِمْ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amri sababi majīʾihim
sentences.l: This is what was of the matter of the cause of their coming.
sentences.i: So much for how they came to be there.
sentences.n: The storyteller’s switch-formula: hādhā mā kāna min amri …, wa-ammā mā kāna min amri …, “so much for …; as for …”.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْعَجُوزِ ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي فَإِنَّهَا لَمَّا أَوْقَعَتِ السُّلْطَانَ ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ وَأَخَاهُ شَرْكَانَ وَالْوَزِيرَ دَنْدَانَ فِي أَيْدِى الْكُفَّارِ أَخَذَتْ تِلْكَ الْعَاهِرَةُ جَوَادًا وَرَكِبَتْهُ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amri al-ʿajūzi dhāti al-dawāhī fa-innahā lammā awqaʿati al-sulṭāna ḍawʾa al-makāni wa-akhāhu sharrukāna wa-al-wazīra dandāna fī aydī al-kuffāri akhadhat tilka al-ʿāhiratu jawādan wa-rakibathu
sentences.l: And as for what was of the matter of the old-woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī: when she had made-fall the sultan Ḍawʾ al-Makān and his brother Sharrukān and the vizier Dandān into the hands of the infidels, that harlot took a steed and mounted it,
sentences.i: As for the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī: once she had delivered the sultan Ḍawʾ al-Makān, his brother Sharrukān and the vizier Dandān into the hands of the infidels, that harlot took a horse and mounted it,
sentences.n: awqaʿa fī, “make fall into”, is to betray someone into a trap.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لِلْكُفَّارِ إِنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَلْحَقَ عَسْكَرَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَأَتَحَيَّلَ عَلَى هَلَاكِهِمْ لِأَنَّهُمْ فِى الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ فَأُعْلِمُهُمْ أَنَّ أَصْحَابَهُمْ هَلَكُوا
sentences.tr: wa-qālat li-al-kuffāri innī urīdu an alḥaqa ʿaskara al-muslimīna wa-ataḥayyala ʿalā halākihim li-annahum fī al-qusṭanṭīniyyati fa-uʿlimuhum anna aṣḥābahum halakū
sentences.l: and said to the infidels: I want that I overtake the army of the Muslims and contrive for their destruction, because they are at Constantinople; and I will inform them that their companions have perished.
sentences.i: and said to the infidels, “I mean to catch up with the Muslim army, which is at Constantinople, and contrive their ruin. I will tell them that their comrades are dead,
sentences.n: li-al-kuffāri, “to the infidels”: li- marks whom she speaks to. taḥayyala ʿalā, “use guile against, plot”: the verb chooses the ʿalā. li-annahum, “because they …”: she must go to them because that is where they are.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا سَمِعُوا ذَلِكَ مِنِّي تَشَتَّتَ شَمْلُهُمْ وَانْصَرَمَ حَبْلُهُمْ وَتَفَرَّقَ جَمْعُهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā samiʿū dhālika minnī tashattata shamluhum wa-inṣarama ḥabluhum wa-tafarraqa jamʿuhum
sentences.l: And when they hear that from me, their union will be-scattered, and their rope will be-cut, and their gathering will be-dispersed.
sentences.i: and when they hear it from me, their ranks will break, their bond will snap and their host will scatter.
sentences.n: Three rhyming clauses on -uhum, the storyteller’s stock phrases for an army falling apart; ḥabl, “rope”, is the tie that holds them together.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَدْخُلُ أَنَا إِلَى الْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ مَلِكِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ وَوَلَدِي الْمَلِكِ حَرْدُوبَ مَلِكِ الرُّومِ وَأُخْبِرُهُمَا بِهَذَا الْخَبَرِ فَيَخْرُجَانِ بِعَسَاكِرِهِمَا إِلَى الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَيُهْلِكُونَهُمْ وَلَا يَتْرُكُونَ أَحَدًا مِنْهُمْ
sentences.tr: thumma adkhulu anā ilā al-maliki afrīdūna maliki al-qusṭanṭīniyyati wa-waladī al-maliki ḥardūba maliki al-rūmi wa-ukhbiruhumā bi-hādhā al-khabari fa-yakhrujāni bi-ʿasākirihimā ilā al-muslimīna wa-yuhlikūnahum wa-lā yatrukūna aḥadan minhum
sentences.l: Then I go in, I, to King Afrīdūn, king of Constantinople, and my son King Ḥardūb, king of the Rūm, and inform them-two of this news; and they-two go out with their-two armies to the Muslims, and they destroy them and do not leave one of them.
sentences.i: Then I will go in to King Afrīdūn, king of Constantinople, and to my son King Ḥardūb, king of the Rūm, and give them this news; and they will march out with their armies against the Muslims, destroy them, and leave not one of them alive.”
sentences.n: akhbara bi-, “inform of”: the verb chooses the bi-. kharaja bi-, “go out with, lead out”: bi- of what they take along. The verbs go from dual (yakhrujāni, the two kings) to plural (yuhlikūnahum, kings and armies together).

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا سَارَتْ تَقْطَعُ الْأَرْضَ عَلَى ذَلِكَ الْجَوَادِ طُولَ اللَّيْلِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā sārat taqṭaʿu al-arḍa ʿalā dhālika al-jawādi ṭūla al-layli
sentences.l: Then she went, cutting the earth on that steed the length of the night.
sentences.i: Then she set off, covering the ground on that horse all night long.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ لَاحَ لَهَا عَسْكَرُ بَهْرَامَ وَرُسْتُمَ فَدَخَلَتْ بَعْضَ الْغَابَاتِ وَأَخْفَتْ جَوَادَهَا هُنَاكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu lāḥa lahā ʿaskaru bahrāma wa-rustuma fa-dakhalat baʿḍa al-ghābāti wa-akhfat jawādahā hunāka
sentences.l: And when the morning became-morning, there appeared to her the army of Bahrām and Rustam; and she entered some of the thickets and hid her steed there.
sentences.i: When morning came, the army of Bahrām and Rustam came into sight; she went into a thicket and hid her horse there.
sentences.n: lāḥa li-, “appear to, loom before”: li- of the one who sees.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ خَرَجَتْ وَتَمَشَّتْ قَلِيلًا وَهِيَ تَقُولُ فِي نَفْسِهَا لَعَلَّ عَسَاكِرَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ قَدْ رَجَعُوا مُنْهَزِمِينَ مِنْ حَرْبِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: thumma kharajat wa-tamashshat qalīlan wa-hiya taqūlu fī nafsihā laʿalla ʿasākira al-muslimīna qad rajaʿū munhazimīna min ḥarbi al-qusṭanṭīniyyati
sentences.l: Then she came-out and walked a little, she saying in herself: Perhaps the armies of the Muslims have returned routed from the war of Constantinople.
sentences.i: Then she came out and walked on a little, saying to herself, “Perhaps the Muslim armies have been routed in the war at Constantinople and are on their way back.”

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا قَرُبَتْ مِنْهُمْ نَظَرَتْ إِلَيْهِمْ وَتَحَقَّقَتْ أَعْلَامَهُمْ فَرَأَتْهَا غَيْرَ مُنَكَّسَةٍ فَعَلِمَتْ أَنَّهُمْ أَتَوْا غَيْرَ مُنْهَزِمِينَ وَلَا خَائِفِينَ عَلَى مَلِكِهِمْ وَأَصْحَابِهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā qarubat minhum naẓarat ilayhim wa-taḥaqqaqat aʿlāmahum fa-raʾathā ghayra munakkasatin fa-ʿalimat annahum ataw ghayra munhazimīna wa-lā khāʾifīna ʿalā malikihim wa-aṣḥābihim
sentences.l: And when she drew-near to them, she looked at them and made-certain-of their banners, and saw them not lowered-head-down; and she knew that they had come not routed, nor fearing for their king and their companions.
sentences.i: When she came near them, she looked them over and made out their banners clearly, and saw that they were not lowered; so she knew they had come neither routed nor in fear for their king and comrades.
sentences.n: A banner munakkasa, “turned upside down”, is a sign of defeat or mourning. khāfa ʿalā, “fear for (someone)”: the verb chooses the ʿalā.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا عَايَنَتْ ذَلِكَ أَسْرَعَتْ نَحْوَهُمْ بِالْجَرْيِ الشَّدِيدِ مِثْلَ الشَّيْطَانِ الْمَرِيدِ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلَتْ إِلَيْهِمْ وَقَالَتْ لَهُمُ الْعَجَلَ الْعَجَلَ يَا جُنْدَ الرَّحْمٰنِ إِلَى جِهَادِ حِزْبِ الشَّيْطَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ʿāyanat dhālika asraʿat naḥwahum bi-al-jaryi al-shadīdi mithla al-shayṭāni al-marīdi ilā an waṣalat ilayhim wa-qālat lahumu al-ʿajala al-ʿajala yā junda al-raḥmāni ilā jihādi ḥizbi al-shayṭāni
sentences.l: And when she beheld that, she hastened toward them with the hard running, like the rebellious devil, until she reached them, and she said to them: Haste, haste, O army of the Merciful, to the holy-war against the party of the devil!
sentences.i: Seeing this, she sped toward them at a run, like a rebel devil, until she reached them and cried, “Make haste, make haste, soldiers of the Merciful, to war against the devil’s party!”
sentences.n: bi-al-jaryi, “with running”: bi- of the manner. al-shayṭān al-marīd, “the rebellious devil”, is Qurʾānic (Q 37:7). al-ʿajala is the accusative of urging. ḥizb al-shayṭān, “the party of Satan”, is also Qurʾānic (Q 58:19). Sajʿ: al-shadīdi/al-marīdi, al-raḥmāni/al-shayṭāni.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهَا بَهْرَامُ أَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهَا وَتَرَجَّلَ وَقَبَّلَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا وَقَالَ لَهَا يَا وَلِيَّ اللَّهِ مَا وَرَاءَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhā bahrāmu aqbala ʿalayhā wa-tarajjala wa-qabbala al-arḍa bayna yadayhā wa-qāla lahā yā waliyya allāhi mā warāʾaka
sentences.l: And when Bahrām saw her, he came-forward to her and dismounted and kissed the ground between her two hands, and said to her: O friend of God, what is behind you?
sentences.i: When Bahrām saw her, he came up to her, dismounted, kissed the ground before her and said, “Holy man of God, what news do you bring?”
sentences.n: The narrator calls the old woman “her”, but Bahrām takes her for the ascetic she is dressed as and addresses a man: waliyy allāh, “friend of God”, a saint, and the masculine -ka. mā warāʾaka, “what is behind you?”, asks what news one brings.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَاتَسْأَلْ عَنْ سُوءِ الْحَالِ وَشَدِيدِ الْأَ هْوَالِ فَإِنَّ أَصْحَابَنَا لَمَّا أَخَذُوا الْمَالَ مِنْ دَيْرِ مَطَرْ وَحَنَّى أَرَادُوا أَنْ يَتَوَجَّهُوا إِلَى الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ خَرَجَ عَلَيْهِمْ عَسْكَرٌ جَرَّارٌ ذُو بَأْسٍ مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lā tasʾal ʿan sūʾi al-ḥāli wa-shadīdi al-ahwāli fa-inna aṣḥābanā lammā akhadhū al-māla min dayri maṭar wa-ḥannā arādū an yatawajjahū ilā al-qusṭanṭīniyyati fa-ʿinda dhālika kharaja ʿalayhim ʿaskarun jarrārun dhū baʾsin mina al-kuffāri
sentences.l: And he said: Do not ask about the evil of the state and the severe of the terrors; for our companions, when they had taken the wealth from the Monastery of Maṭar wa-Ḥannā, wanted to turn-toward Constantinople, and at that there came-out against them a huge army, possessor of might, of the infidels.
sentences.i: She said, “Do not ask how bad things are, how dire the dangers! When our comrades had taken the treasure from the Monastery of Maṭar wa-Ḥannā and meant to make for Constantinople, a vast and formidable army of infidels sallied out against them.”
sentences.n: “He said”: the narrative follows the disguise and speaks of the old woman as the male ascetic, so the masculine qāla is right here. The print runs لا and تسال together (لاتسال) and splits الاهوال, al-ahwāl, “the terrors”, into الا هوال; the spacing is kept both times. The monastery’s name is printed as two words and given as printed. kharaja ʿalā, “come out against, attack”: the verb chooses the ʿalā. jarrār, “dragging”, is said of an army so large it seems to drag along the ground. Sajʿ: al-ḥāli/al-ahwāli.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلْعُونَةَ أَعَادَتْ إِلَيْهِمُ الْحَدِيثَ إِرْجَافًا وَوَجَلًا وَقَالَتْ إِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ هَلَكَ وَلَمْ يَبْقَ مِنْهُمْ إِلَّا خَمْسَةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ رَجُلًا
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malʿūnata aʿādat ilayhimu al-ḥadītha irjāfan wa-wajalan wa-qālat inna aktharahum halaka wa-lam yabqa minhum illā khamsatun wa-ʿishrūna rajulan
sentences.l: Then the accursed one repeated to them the story, by-way-of alarm-spreading and fear, and said: The most of them perished, and there did not remain of them except five and twenty men.
sentences.i: Then the accursed woman told them the tale over again, to spread alarm and dread, and said that most of them had perished and no more than twenty-five men were left.
sentences.n: irjāf is the spreading of disquieting rumours, especially of defeat; the accusatives say why she told it. halaka, singular, after aktharahum, “most of them”, agrees with the word akthar.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ بَهْرَامُ أَيُّهَا الزَّاهِدُ مَتَى فَارَقْتَهُمْ فَقَالَ فِي لَيْلَتِي هَذِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla bahrāmu ayyuhā al-zāhidu matā fāraqtahum fa-qāla fī laylatī hādhihi
sentences.l: And Bahrām said: O you the ascetic, when did you part-from them? And he said: In this night of mine.
sentences.i: Bahrām said, “Holy ascetic, when did you leave them?” “This very night,” she replied.
sentences.n: al-zāhid, “the ascetic”, masculine, is the part the old woman is playing; hence the masculine fāraqta and fa-qāla.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ بَهْرَامُ سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي طَوَى لَكَ الْأَرْضَ الْبَعِيدَةَ وَأَنْتَ مَاشٍ عَلَى قَدَمَيْكَ مُتَّكِئًا عَلَى جَرِيدَةٍ لَكِنَّكَ مِنَ الْأَوْلِيَاءِ الطَّيَّارَةِ الْمُلْهَمِينَ وَحْيَ الْإِشَارَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla bahrāmu subḥāna alladhī ṭawā laka al-arḍa al-baʿīdata wa-anta māshin ʿalā qadamayka muttakiʾan ʿalā jarīdatin lākinnaka mina al-awliyāʾi al-ṭayyārati al-mulhamīna waḥya al-ishārati
sentences.l: And Bahrām said: Glory to the One who folded-up for you the far land, while you are walking on your two feet, leaning on a palm-rod! But you are of the saints, the flying-ones, the inspired-ones with the revelation of the sign.
sentences.i: Bahrām said, “Glory to Him who folded up the far-off earth for you, though you go on foot, leaning on a palm-staff! But then you are one of the flying saints, those inspired by revelation through signs.”
sentences.n: ṭawā al-arḍa, “folded up the earth”: ṭayy al-arḍ is the miracle credited to saints of crossing great distances in a moment. laka, “for you”: li- of the one it was done for. al-ṭayyāra, “the fliers”, is an intensive form with the feminine ending, used collectively for a class of people. The phrase al-mulhamīna waḥya al-ishārati is compressed, “inspired with the revelation of the sign”; it seems to mean saints to whom God speaks by hints. Sajʿ: al-ṭayyārati/al-ishārati.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ رَكِبَ عَلَى ظَهْرِ جَوَادِهِ وَهُوَ مَدْهُوشٌ حَيْرَانُ بِمَا سَمِعَهُ مِنْ ذَاتِ الْإِفْكِ وَالْبُهْتَانِ وَقَالَ لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ لَقَدْ ضَاعَ تَعَبُنَا وَضَاقَتْ صُدُورُنَا وَأُسِرَ سُلْطَانُنَا وَمَنْ مَعَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma rakiba ʿalā ẓahri jawādihi wa-huwa madhūshun ḥayrānu bi-mā samiʿahu min dhāti al-ifki wa-al-buhtāni wa-qāla lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-allāhi laqad ḍāʿa taʿabunā wa-ḍāqat ṣudūrunā wa-usira sulṭānunā wa-man maʿahu
sentences.l: Then he mounted on the back of his steed, and he was dazed, bewildered by what he had heard from the possessor of the lie and the slander, and said: There is no power and no strength except in God! Our toil has been lost, and our breasts have become-narrow, and our sultan has been captured, and whoever is with him.
sentences.i: Then he mounted his horse, dazed and bewildered by what he had heard from that mistress of lies and slander, and said, “There is no power and no strength save in God! All our toil is lost, our hearts are heavy, and our sultan has been taken captive, and those with him.”
sentences.n: dhāt al-ifk wa-al-buhtān, “she of the lie and the slander”, plays on her name, Dhāt al-Dawāhī, “she of the calamities”. bi-mā, “by what”: bi- of the cause. In lā ḥawla … illā bi-allāhi, bi- means “through, in”: all power is God’s. ḍāqa al-ṣadr, “the breast grew narrow”, is to be distressed. The print marks the alif of واُسر with a ḍamma: usira, passive.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ جَعَلُوا يَقْطَعُونَ الْأَرْضَ طُولًا وَعَرْضًا لَيْلًا وَنَهَارًا
sentences.tr: thumma jaʿalū yaqṭaʿūna al-arḍa ṭūlan wa-ʿarḍan laylan wa-nahāran
sentences.l: Then they began to cut-across the land in length and in breadth, by night and by day.
sentences.i: Then they set about crossing the land far and wide, night and day.
sentences.n: jaʿala with a present verb is “begin to, set about”. ṭūlan wa-ʿarḍan, “lengthwise and crosswise”, and laylan wa-nahāran, “night and day”, are adverbial accusatives.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ وَقْتُ السَّحَرِ أَقْبَلُوا عَلَي رأْسِ الشِّعْبِ فَرأَوْا ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ وَأَخَاهُ شَرْكَانَ يُنَادِيَانِ بِالتَّهْلِيلِ وَالتَّكْبِيرِ وَالصَّلَوٰةِ وَالسَّلَامِ عَلَى الْبَشِيرِ النَّذِيرِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna waqtu al-saḥari aqbalū ʿalā raʾsi al-shiʿbi fa-raʾaw ḍawʾa al-makāni wa-akhāhu sharrukāna yunādiyāni bi-al-tahlīli wa-al-takbīri wa-al-ṣalāti wa-al-salāmi ʿalā al-bashīri al-nadhīri
sentences.l: And when it was the time of the before-dawn, they came-upon the head of the pass, and they saw Ḍawʾ al-Makān and his brother Sharrukān calling-out with the tahlīl and the takbīr and the blessing and the peace upon the bringer-of-good-news, the warner.
sentences.i: Just before dawn they came out at the head of the pass, and there they saw Ḍawʾ al-Makān and his brother Sharrukān crying aloud “There is no god but God” and “God is greatest”, and calling blessings and peace upon the Bearer of good tidings, the Warner.
sentences.n: aqbala ʿalā, “come up to, arrive at”: the verb chooses the ʿalā, which the print spells here with a dotted yāʾ (علي); it is read ʿalā. yunādiyāni is dual, for the two brothers; nādā bi-, “call out (a cry)”: bi- of the words cried. The formulas are those of the opening of this night. al-ṣalāt is printed الصلوة, the old Qurʾānic spelling; the dagger alif is ours.

sentences.t: فَحَمَلَ هُوَ وَأَصْحَابُهُ وَأَحَاطُوا بِالْكُفَّارِ إِحَاطَةَ السَّيْلِ بِالْقِفَارِ وَصَاحُوا عَلَيْهِمْ صِيَاحًا ضَجَّتْ مِنْهُ الْأَبْطَالُ وَتَصَدَّعَتْ بِهِ الْجِبَالُ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥamala huwa wa-aṣḥābuhu wa-aḥāṭū bi-al-kuffāri iḥāṭata al-sayli bi-al-qifāri wa-ṣāḥū ʿalayhim ṣiyāḥan ḍajjat minhu al-abṭālu wa-taṣaddaʿat bihi al-jibālu
sentences.l: And he charged, he and his companions, and they surrounded the infidels as the torrent surrounds the wastes, and they shouted at them a shouting from which the champions clamoured and by which the mountains were split.
sentences.i: He and his men charged and closed round the infidels as a flood closes round the desert waste, and raised against them a shout that set the champions clamouring and split the mountains.
sentences.n: “He” is the commander of the relief column, Bahrām. Rhymed prose: al-kuffāri / al-qifāri, then al-abṭālu / al-jibālu. aḥāṭa bi-, “surround”: the verb chooses the bi-, used twice (bi-al-kuffāri, bi-al-qifāri). iḥāṭata al-sayli and ṣiyāḥan are cognate accusatives: “a surrounding like the torrent’s”, “a shouting”. ṣāḥa ʿalā, “shout at”. taṣaddaʿat bihi, “were split by it”: bi- of the cause.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ وَأَشْرَقَ بِنُورِهِ وَلَاحَ فَاحَ لَهُمْ مِنْ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ طِيبُهُ وَنَشْرُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu wa-ashraqa bi-nūrihi wa-lāḥa fāḥa lahum min ḍawʾi al-makāni ṭībuhu wa-nashruhu
sentences.l: And when the morning became-morning and shone with its light and gleamed, there wafted to them from Ḍawʾ al-Makān his fragrance and his scent.
sentences.i: When morning broke and shone out in its light and gleamed, the fragrance and sweet scent of Ḍawʾ al-Makān came wafting to them.
sentences.n: The print has بنورة, a misprint for بنوره, corrected here. The daybreak formula again, now rhyming on to fāḥa. Ḍawʾ al-Makān means “Light of the Place”, so the dawn and the prince arrive together. The fragrance that “wafts” from a hero is a stock way of saying his presence is felt.

sentences.t: وَتَعَارَفُوا بِبَعْضِهِمْ كَمَاتَقَدَّمَ ذِكْرُهُ فَقَبَّلُوا الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَأَخِيهِ شَرْكَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-taʿārafū bi-baʿḍihim ka-mā taqaddama dhikruhu fa-qabbalū al-arḍa bayna yaday ḍawʾi al-makāni wa-akhīhi sharrukāna
sentences.l: And they made-acquaintance with one-another, as its mention has gone-before, and they kissed the ground between the two hands of Ḍawʾ al-Makān and his brother Sharrukān.
sentences.i: They made themselves known to one another, as told before, and kissed the ground before Ḍawʾ al-Makān and his brother Sharrukān.
sentences.n: The print runs كما and تقدم together (كماتقدم); the spacing is kept. taʿārafa is already “know one another”; adding bi-baʿḍihim, “with one another”, is a colloquial doubling, where bi- marks the partner. bayna yaday, “between the two hands of”, is “in the presence of”.

sentences.t: وَأَخْبَرَهُمْ شَرْكَانُ بِمَا جَرَى لَهُمْ فِي الْمَغَارَةِ فَتَعَجَّبُوا مِنْ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-akhbarahum sharrukānu bi-mā jarā lahum fī al-maghārati fa-taʿajjabū min dhālika
sentences.l: And Sharrukān informed them of what had happened to them in the cave, and they marvelled at that.
sentences.i: Sharrukān told them what had befallen them in the cave, and they marvelled at it.
sentences.n: akhbara bi-, “inform of”: the verb chooses the bi-. taʿajjaba min, “marvel at”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالُوا لِبَعْضِهِمْ أَسْرِعُوا بِنَا إِلَى الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ لِأَنَّنَا تَرَكْنَا أَصْحَابَنَا هُنَاكَ وَقُلُوبُنَا عِنْدَهُمْ
sentences.tr: thumma qālū li-baʿḍihim asriʿū binā ilā al-qusṭanṭīniyyati li-annanā taraknā aṣḥābanā hunāka wa-qulūbunā ʿindahum
sentences.l: Then they said to one-another: Hasten with us to Constantinople, because we left our companions there and our hearts are with them.
sentences.i: Then they said to one another, “Let us make haste to Constantinople, for we left our comrades there, and our hearts are with them.”
sentences.n: asriʿū binā, literally “hurry with us”, is the usual way of saying “let us hurry”: bi- of company. li-baʿḍihim: li- marks whom they speak to.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَسْرَعُوا فِي الْمَسِيرِ وَتَوَكَّلُوا عَلَى اللَّطِيفِ الْخَبِيرِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika asraʿū fī al-masīri wa-tawakkalū ʿalā al-laṭīfi al-khabīri
sentences.l: And at that they hastened in the march and put-their-trust in the Subtle, the All-Aware.
sentences.i: At that they pressed on with all speed, putting their trust in the Gracious, the All-Aware.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-masīri / al-khabīri. al-Laṭīf and al-Khabīr, “the Subtle (or Kind)” and “the All-Aware”, are two of the names of God, paired in the Qurʾān (e.g. Q 6:103). tawakkala ʿalā, “trust in”: the verb chooses the ʿalā.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ يُقَوِّى الْمُسْلِمِينَ عَلَى الثَّبَاتِ وَيُنْشِدُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna ḍawʾu al-makāni yuqawwī al-muslimīna ʿalā al-thabāti wa-yunshidu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān was strengthening the Muslims to the standing-firm and reciting these verses:
sentences.i: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān kept heartening the Muslims to stand firm, and recited these verses:
sentences.n: Rhymed prose leads into the poem: al-thabāti / al-abyāta. qawwā ʿalā, “strengthen for”: ʿalā of what they are strengthened to do. The print spells yuqawwī with final ى.

sentences.t:
لَكَ الْحَمْدُ يَامُسْتَوْجِبَ الْحَمْدِ وَالشُّكْرِ * فَمَا زِلْتَ لِي بِالْعَوْنِ يَارَبِّ فِي اَمْرِي
رَبَّيْتَ غَرِيْبًا فِي الْبِلَادِ وَكُنْتَ لِي * كَفِيْلاً وَقَدْ قَدَّرْتَ لِيْ نَصْرِيْ
وَاَعْطَيْتَنِي مَالاً وَمُلْكًا وَنِعْمَةً * وَقَلَّدْتَنِي سَيْفَ الشُّجَّاعَةِ وَالنَّصْرِ
وَخَوَّلْتَنِي ظِلَّ الْمَلِيْكِ مُعَمَّرًا * وَقَدْ جُدْتَ لِي مِنْ فَيْضِ جُوْدِكَ بِالْغَمْرِ
وَسَلِمْتَنِي مِنْ كُلِّ خَطْبٍ حَذَرْتُهُ * بِمَشْوَرَةِ الصَّدْرِ الْوَزِيْرِ فَتَى الدَّهْرِى
بِفَضْلِكَ قَدْ صُلْنَا عَلَى الرُّوْمِ صَوْلَةً * وَقَدْ رَجَعُوْا بِالضَّرْبِ فِي حُلَلٍ حُمْرِ
وَاَظْهَرْتُ اِنِّي قَدْ هُزِمْتُ هَزِيْمَةً * وَعُدْتُ عَلَيْهِمْ عَوْدَةَ الضَّيْغَمِ الْغَمْرِ
تَرَكْتُهُمْ فِى الْقَاعِ صَرْعَى كَاَنَّهُمْ * نَشَاوَى بِكَأْسِ الْمَوْتِ لَا قَهْوَةِ الْخَمْرِ
وَصَارَتْ بِاَيْدِيْنَا الْمَرَاكِبُ كُلُّهَا * وَصَارَ لَنَا السُّلْطَانُ فِى الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ
وَجَاءَ اِلَيْنَا الزَّاهِدُ الْعَابِدُ الَّذِيْ * كَرَامَتُهُ شَاعَتْ لَدَى الْبَدْوِ وَالْحَضْرِ
اَتَيْنَا لِاَخْذِ الثَّارِ مِنْ كُلِّ كَافِرِ * وَقَدْ شَاعَ عِنْدَ النَّاسِ مَا كَانَ مِنْ اَمْرِي
وَقَدْ قَتَلُوْا مِنَّا رِجَالًا فَاَصْبَحُوْا * لَهُمْ غُرَفٌ فِي الْخُلْدِ تَعْلُوْ عَلَى نَهْرِ
sentences.tr:
laka al-ḥamdu yā mustawjiba al-ḥamdi wa-al-shukri * fa-mā zilta lī bi-al-ʿawni yā rabbi fī amrī
rabbayta gharīban fī al-bilādi wa-kunta lī * kafīlan wa-qad qaddarta lī naṣrī
wa-aʿṭaytanī mālan wa-mulkan wa-niʿmatan * wa-qalladtanī sayfa al-shujjāʿati wa-al-naṣri
wa-khawwaltanī ẓilla al-malīki muʿammaran * wa-qad judta lī min fayḍi jūdika bi-al-ghamri
wa-salimtanī min kulli khaṭbin ḥadhartuhu * bi-mashwarati al-ṣadri al-wazīri fatā al-dahrī
bi-faḍlika qad ṣulnā ʿalā al-rūmi ṣawlatan * wa-qad rajaʿū bi-al-ḍarbi fī ḥulalin ḥumri
wa-aẓhartu innī qad huzimtu hazīmatan * wa-ʿudtu ʿalayhim ʿawdata al-ḍayghami al-ghamri
taraktuhum fī al-qāʿi ṣarʿā ka-annahum * nashāwā bi-kaʾsi al-mawti lā qahwati al-khamri
wa-ṣārat bi-aydīnā al-marākibu kulluhā * wa-ṣāra lanā al-sulṭānu fī al-barri wa-al-baḥri
wa-jāʾa ilaynā al-zāhidu al-ʿābidu alladhī * karāmatuhu shāʿat ladā al-badwi wa-al-ḥaḍri
ataynā li-akhdhi al-thāri min kulli kāfiri * wa-qad shāʿa ʿinda al-nāsi mā kāna min amrī
wa-qad qatalū minnā rijālan fa-aṣbaḥū * lahum ghurafun fī al-khuldi taʿlū ʿalā nahri
sentences.l:
To you the praise, O deserver of the praise and the thanks; * for you have not ceased, for me, with the help, O my Lord, in my affair.
You reared a stranger in the lands, and you were for me * a guarantor, and you have decreed for me my victory.
And you gave me wealth and kingship and favour, * and you girded me with the sword of the courage and the victory.
And you granted me the shade of the king, long-lived, * and you have been bountiful to me, out of the overflow of your bounty, with the abundance.
And you kept me safe from every calamity I feared * by the counsel of the chief-man, the vizier, the young-hero of the age.
By your grace we have assailed the Rūm with an assault, * and they have gone back, by the striking, in robes red.
And I made-a-show that I had been routed with a rout, * and I turned back upon them with the turning of the lion, the overwhelming.
I left them on the plain, thrown-down, as though they were * drunken-ones with the cup of death, not the draught of the wine.
And the ships came into our hands, all of them, * and the dominion became ours on the land and the sea.
And there came to us the ascetic, the worshipper, whose * wonder-working spread among the nomads and the settled.
We came for the taking of the blood-vengeance from every unbeliever, * and what came of my affair has spread among the people.
And they killed of us men, and these became * having chambers in the Everlasting that rise above a river.
sentences.i:
Praise be to You, who alone deserve all praise and thanks; * You have never ceased to help me, Lord, in all I do.
You reared me, a stranger in the lands, and stood * my guarantor, and You decreed my victory.
You gave me wealth and kingship and good fortune, * and girded me with the sword of courage and of triumph.
You granted me the shelter of a long-lived king, * and lavished on me the flood of Your bounty.
You kept me safe from every peril that I feared, * by the counsel of the vizier, our chief, the hero of the age.
By Your grace we fell upon the Rūm in one great charge, * and they went back, from our blows, in robes of red.
I feigned that I was routed, put to flight, * then turned on them as turns the mighty lion.
I left them in the hollow, strewn like men * drunk on the cup of death, not on the wine.
The ships, all of them, came into our hands, * and ours became the mastery on land and sea.
Then came to us the ascetic, the devout, whose * holy wonders were the talk of town and desert.
We came to take our vengeance on each unbeliever, * and all that I have done is spread among mankind.
They killed men of ours, but those men now possess * high chambers in the Everlasting Garden, rising over a river.
sentences.n: The verse is pointed by the print and copied as printed. يامستوجب is run together; in line 7 the print points اِنِّي (innī) where annī, after aẓhartu, is expected; in line 2 the second half-line is short of the metre, as though words had dropped out, and rabbayta gharīban, “you reared a stranger”, means the poet himself. In line 3 the print doubles the jīm of الشجاعة (al-shujjāʿa), for the usual al-shajāʿa, “courage”. In line 5 وَسَلِمْتَنِي (salimtanī, “you were safe me”) makes no sense; the sense wants sallamtanī, “you kept me safe”; ḥadhartuhu has fatḥa where ḥadhirtuhu is usual; and الدَّهْرِى adds a yāʾ to rhyme with the -rī of the other lines. The vizier of line 5 is Dandān. al-ghamr closes both line 4 (“abundance”) and line 7, where of a lion it is perhaps “overwhelming”, a repeated rhyme word. qahwa, line 8, is an old word for wine, not coffee. The ascetic of line 10 is the disguised old woman whose trap the brothers have only just escaped: the poem praises her in all innocence. The chambers rising over a river echo the Qurʾān’s promise of high chambers in Paradise with rivers flowing beneath (Q 39:20). الثار is printed without hamza (al-thaʾr).

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ ضَوْءُالْمَكَانِ مِنْ شِعْرِهِ هَنَّأَهُ أَخُوهُ شَرْكَانُ بِالسَّلَامَةِ وَشَكَرَهُ عَلَى أَفْعَالِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha ḍawʾu al-makāni min shiʿrihi hannaʾahu akhūhu sharrukānu bi-al-salāmati wa-shakarahu ʿalā afʿālihi
sentences.l: And when Ḍawʾ al-Makān finished from his poetry, his brother Sharrukān congratulated him on the safety and thanked him for his deeds.
sentences.i: When Ḍawʾ al-Makān had finished his poem, his brother Sharrukān congratulated him on his safe deliverance and thanked him for all he had done.
sentences.n: The print runs ضوء and المكان together (ضوءالمكان); the spacing is kept. faragha min, “finish”. hannaʾa bi-, “congratulate on”: the verb chooses the bi-. shakara ʿalā, “thank for”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ تَوَجَّهُوا مُجِدِّينَ الْمَسِيرَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahum tawajjahū mujiddīna al-masīra
sentences.l: Then they set-out, pressing-hard the march.
sentences.i: Then they set off, pushing on in haste.
sentences.n: mujiddīna al-masīra, “urging on the march”: ajadda al-sayra, “make haste on a journey”, takes its object directly.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The print sets the name as two words here, شهر زاد; the spacing is kept.
